xmldoc.short_description: Write the neutral struct to an ISHNE 1.0 Holter ECG file.

param_input_item.param_description: a struct from ishne.read, or one built by hand with the same fields.
a numeric matrix, one column per lead.
the sampling rate in hertz, one positive number.
with 'Leads', one lead name per column; by default lead1, lead2 and so on.
with 'Resolution', the nanovolts per step, one value or one per lead (default 1000, one microvolt per step).
with 'Physical', a logical saying SAMPLES is in millivolts and is quantised with the resolution; by default SAMPLES is the raw integers the file stores.

param_output_item.param_description: what was laid down: the number of leads, the number of samples, the rate and the file written.

description.p: The one writer of the ISHNE 1.0 Holter ECG binary format. It lays down a file any tool can read and this module reads back. Given a struct from ishne.read with raw integer samples, what is read back equals what went in, to the bit, checksum included.

Passed a plain matrix with a rate instead of a struct, it fills the header with defaults and names the leads lead1, lead2 and so on unless 'Leads' names them. With 'Physical', true the millivolts are quantised to the raw integer the file holds, raw = round(mV * 1e6 / resolution).

xmldoc.bibliography: Badilini, The ISHNE Holter standard output file format, Annals of Noninvasive Electrocardiology 3(3), 1998.

example_item.example_item_data: samples = round(1000 * sin(2 * pi * (0:2499)' / 250)); ishne.write('out.ecg', samples, 250, 'Leads', {'I'});
